label: Born in Tampere, Finland
Completed Matriculation examinations in Turku
Began electrical engineering studies at HUT
VTT Semiconductor Laboratory established within Stubb's HUT lab
Completed Master's thesis on Schottky diodes for radar detectors
Proposed and began study of Ovonic picosecond switches under Stubb
description: As assistant teacher at HUT, Suntola got Stubb's approval to investigate amorphous chalcogenide switches; the work later became his doctoral thesis.

label: Licentiate's thesis on chalcogenide switching mechanism
Doctor of Science in Technology at age 28
description: Youngest Doctor of Science in Technology from the HUT Electrical Engineering department by that time, on chalcogenide thin film switching.

label: Assigned Vaisala humidity sensor development at VTT Semiconductor Laboratory
description: The laboratory's first industrial order, from Vaisala Oy, was assigned by Stubb to Suntola, with Tapio Wiik making the pre-study.

label: Humidity sensor patent priority date
Nominated docent at Tampere University of Technology
description: Invited to lecture on semiconductor physics at TUT, continuing every second Friday for a couple of years.

label: Thin polymer film humidity sensor (Humicap) completed with Antson
Contacted by Instrumentarium top management to set up research group
description: After Datex's key technical team left, Suntola was invited to establish a research group under Instrumentarium with an open request to 'suggest and find out something'.

label: Moved with humidity sensor team from VTT to Instrumentarium, Tapiola
Invention of atomic layer epitaxy
description: Idea of sequentially 'serving' complementary elements of a compound one at a time onto a surface, conceived while looking at the Periodic Table in an empty laboratory.

sources.quote: Looking at the Periodic Table, and thinking of the overall symmetry in nature, to me came the idea of "serving" the complementary elements of a compound sequentially, one at a time, onto a surface.

label: Design of first carousel ALE reactor completed
description: Drawings of the 12-inch T-piece rotating carousel reactor sent to the in-house mechanical workshop.

label: First ALE growth experiments of ZnS succeed
description: Film grew in the very first experiment at about a third of a monolayer per cycle; XRD at HUT showed hexagonal ZnS.

sources.quote: The very first experiment was successful; a film was observed to grow – not, however at the expected rate, one monolayer in a cycle, but only a third of a monolayer in a cycle.

label: Finnish ALE patent application filed (priority date)

sources.quote: The priority date of the patent comes from the Finnish application, filed on November 29, 1974.

label: Encouraged TUT group to work on ALE of III-V semiconductors
First ALE patent published (US 4,058,430)
Defended ALE patent at hearing in Moscow
description: Suntola went alone, assisted by two local attorneys; no critical prior art was presented and the patent was granted as applied.

label: Contacted Lauri Niinistö for ALE chemistry consultation
ALE-EL project sold by Instrumentarium to Lohja Oy
description: Project, personnel and facility transferred to Lohja, a building material company expanding into electronics.

label: Markus Pessa nominated professor of physics at TUT
First successful ZnCl2 + H2S ALE process in glass tube flow reactor
description: Reactor tube walls evenly covered with a strictly uniform film; Pakkala's reaction 'That's it!' switched development to chloride processes and inert gas reactors.

label: Second ALE patent filed (inert gas reactor and EL processes)
Humidity sensor patent published (US 4,164,868)
First public disclosure of ALE-EL display at SID, San Diego
description: Presentation with a high-contrast EL demonstration box to about 1000 attendees; Lohja afterwards received 3000–4000 product requests.

sources.quote: The presentation was a great success – Suntola had not realized before this, how much their EL technology was ahead of all the competitors.

label: 1980 SID Outstanding Paper Award handed to Suntola's team
ALE talk at ICVGE-5, San Diego; seeds of Japanese ALE research
description: Talk was not a big success and the term 'epitaxy' offended silicon researchers, but Nishizawa in the audience realized the significance of ALE.

label: First ALE reactor supplied to Niinistö's laboratory at HUT
description: Placed in a locked room accessible only to authorized operators; seed of later University of Helsinki ALD activity.

label: Lohja offers ALE semiconductor license to US manufacturer in New York
description: Advantages of ALE for gate dielectrics and passivation were not understood; existing technologies were seen to fulfill the needs.

label: Pilot production of TF-EL displays starts at Lohja's Kunnarla plant
ALE-EL information boards installed at Helsinki-Vantaa airport
description: First real proof of concept; ATO dielectrics chosen after cave tests, boards ran 15 years without a module replacement.

label: ALE-EL license granted to Sintra Alcatel, France
description: Contacts began with CGE at SID 1980; a 450 mm x 450 mm ALE reactor was delivered to France as part of the license.

label: Second ALE patent published (US 4,413,022)
Lohja builds Olarinluoma EL production facility in Espoo
description: Built to exploit government tax reductions for production investments completed by summer 1984.

label: Invited ALE talk at 16th Conf. on Solid State Devices and Materials, Kobe
description: Nishizawa introduced MLE-grown GaAs at the same conference; Suntola spoke to an overfull room and was interviewed by Japanese TV.

label: Ahti Aintila leaves Lohja microelectronics division
First Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy, Espoo
description: Organized by VTT Semiconductor Laboratory upon the initiative of Lauri Niinistö.

label: LCD sequential color display patent applied
EL data display module production starts at Olarinluoma
description: Distribution channels opened in the USA and other industrialized countries; Lohja became the third EL manufacturer after Sharp and Planar.

label: Antti Piippo invited from Aspo to manage Lohja Display Electronics
Suntola continues as Chief Scientist at Lohja
description: Mandate to look for new application areas for ALE as electronics activities were reorganized into a business unit.

label: Suntola sets up Microchemistry Ltd as Neste subsidiary
description: Founded for ALE-based solar panels and heterogeneous catalysis; owned 80% Neste / 20% Lohja, with Lohja's ALE patents licensed for PV and catalysts only.

sources.quote: In 1987, Tuomo Suntola was offered the chance to set up Microchemistry Ltd, as a subsidiary of Neste, for the development of ALE-based solar panels.

label: F-120 research reactor designed – first commercial ALD reactor
description: First task at Microchemistry: Suntola and Lindfors designed a quick, compact reactor for PV development.

label: ALE review paper in Materials Science Reports
description: Mapped known laboratories working on ALE; no information yet on the Soviet molecular layering group.

label: Lohja's EL business sold to Planar Inc.
description: Finnish EL activity became Planar International, a subsidiary of US Planar; all Planar EL production later concentrated in Olarinluoma.

label: Lohja microelectronics division separated as Elcoteq Oy
Neste buys Lohja's share of Microchemistry; ALE license extended
description: License extended to cover manufacturing and sales of ALE reactors and ALE technology for any use not covered by Lohja's EL patents.

label: NAPS acquires a-Si solar panel factory in France
description: Microchemistry was tasked with improving the 3–4% efficiency a-Si production process.

label: LCD color display patent granted (US 4,907,862)
First International Symposium on Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE-1), Espoo
description: Chaired by Lauri Niinistö; Drozd invited Suntola to Leningrad to meet Aleskovskii.

label: Visit to Aleskovskii in Leningrad; ALE and molecular layering connect
description: Aleskovskii presented oxide layer build-up by saturated surface reactions, confirming independent discovery of the essence of ALE.

sources.quote: The discussion confirmed that the essence of ALE had been independently discovered by the Aleskovskii group.

label: Ahti Aintila establishes Picopack Oy
Antti Piippo and colleagues buy Elcoteq
Marina Lindblad doctoral thesis on quantum chemistry of ZnS ALE growth
Suvi Haukka doctoral dissertation on ALE catalysts
ALE-CdTe test cell reaches 14% conversion efficiency
description: Among the highest reported for thin film cells; ALE advantage judged marginal so no production scale-up.

label: ALE for Semiconductor Applications talk and booth at MRS Fall Meeting, Boston
description: Demonstrated uniformity, conformality and high density of ALE Al2O3; actual 8-inch wafers shown at Microchemistry's booth.

label: Arla Kytökivi doctoral dissertation on ALE catalysts
NAPS withdraws from French factory and a-Si technology
Microchemistry refocused on ALE reactors; Suntola offered Neste Research Fellow position
description: PV and catalyst research moved to Neste Central Research; Matti Ervasti invited as business-oriented managing director.

label: Hands Microchemistry over to Ervasti; leaves active role in ALE

sources.quote: When handing Microchemistry Ltd. over to his successor, Matti Ervasti, in the beginning of 1998, Suntola left behind his active role in ALE, now renamed as ALD.

label: Microchemistry sold to ASM; continues as ASM Microchemistry
Part-time retirement from Fortum
Full retirement from Fortum
Sven Lindfors and Kustaa Poutiainen found Picosun Oy
Joins Picosun Oy as scientific adviser
European SEMI Award 2004 at Munich Electronics Show
description: Handed by SEMI President & CEO Stanley Myers; Lindfors and Poutiainen accompanied Suntola.

label: Beneq Oy founded; Pekka Soininen starts ALE reactor activity
Becomes board member of Picosun Oy
Publishes 'The Dynamic Universe' (3rd ed.)
Elcoteq goes bankrupt
Publishes 'The Short History of Science'
Beneq Oy acquires Planar's Olarinluoma EL plant
Invited talk 'From Ideas to Global Industry – 40 Years of ALD in Finland'
